3095._note: HAND-AUTHORED (not BIN-sourced -- raw.communitydragon.org unreachable this session). Quote from https://wiki.leagueoflegends.com/en-us/Kraken_Slayer infobox, fetched live this session: Unique - Bring It Down: 'Basic attacks on-hit grant a stack for 3 seconds, up to 2 stacks. At 2 stacks, the next basic attack consumes all stacks to deal (Melee 150-200 / Ranged 120-160) (based on level) bonus physical damage on-hit, increased by 0%-75% (based on target's missing health), for up to (Melee 262.5-350 / Ranged 210-280) (based on level) bonus physical damage.' The wiki's Patch History shows the base-damage range 150-200/120-160 was set in V14.19 ('Bring It Down base damage changed to (Melee 150-200 / Ranged 120-160) (based on level) from (Melee 140-310 / Ranged 112-248) (based on level)') and the missing-health scaling 0%-75% was set in V25.14 ('Bring It Down bonus damage increased to 0%-75% (based on target's missing health) from 0%-50%'), with no later patch (through V25.16, the latest listed) touching either value, so both are confirmed current as of this session (2026-07-10). The max-damage endpoints (262.5-350/210-280) are exactly base x 1.75 (200x1.75=350, 160x1.75=280 etc.), confirming the formula shape is base x (1 + 0.75 x missingHpFraction), i.e. base + base x 0.75 x missingHpFraction -- a base-plus-scaling-term shape, NOT the project's existing pure fraction x HP-quantity execute shape. COMBO-INTERNAL STACK COUNTING: unlike AurelionSol/Kindred's buff-stack passives (out of scope -- those need real live game-state data the Live Client API doesn't expose), Kraken Slayer's stacking depends only on the SEQUENCE of AA nodes within the combo ComboRunner is already building, so it is computed entirely at combo-assembly time (see ComboRunner.ApplyBinDamage's aaOrdinal counter / ItemTrigger.StackThenConsume): the bonus triggers on every (stacksRequired+1)=3rd AA in the combo's own node order (3rd, 6th, 9th...). This ASSUMES every AA in the combo lands within the real 3-second stack window, which is a reasonable approximation for a short burst combo but would overcount stacks in an unrealistically long/slow one -- documented alongside the existing spellblade 'at most one proc per combo' approximation in ComboRunner.cs. MISSING-HEALTH SCALING NOW MODELED (previously deliberately omitted -- see M05_DAMAGE_ENGINE.md changelog): a new Damage.ExecuteType.BaseWithMissingHpBonus case (base x (1 + scalar x missingHpFraction), the exact confirmed shape) was added rather than forcing this into the pure fraction x HP-quantity mechanism Blade of the Ruined King uses. "missingHpBonusScalar": 0.75 below is that confirmed scalar; ComboRunner.BuildStackThenConsumeItemProc wires it in, using the LIVE target's current/max HP (same dynamic mechanism as Blade of the Ruined King's CurrentHp). STARTING-HP CAVEAT NARROWED, NOT CLOSED (see M05_DAMAGE_ENGINE.md changelog and Combo/TargetHealthTracker.cs): the target's HP at the START of a combo used to always be MaxHP (the Live Client API exposes no enemy current-HP at all); when a TargetHealthTracker is wired in (AppComposition), the starting CurrentHP is instead MaxHP minus an honest LOWER-BOUND estimate (100% HP anchored at the target's last known respawn, minus OUR OWN calculated combo damage dealt to them since) -- this can only ever UNDERSTATE real missing health (potion/elixir/buff healing and non-combo damage sources remain invisible to us), never overstate it, so this proc's missing-HP scaling is now sometimes MORE accurate than before but still never provably exact. Re-check this note against the wiki on any future patch that mentions Kraken Slayer/Bring It Down.
3095.name: Kraken Slayer

3128._note: HAND-AUTHORED from this project's own bundled ddragon/16.13.1/item.json (id 3128, colloq ';dfg', name 'Deathfire Grasp') this session (2026-07-10), user-reported as not applying. Quoted description: 'Active - The Silence: Deal magic damage equal to 15% of the Target's Max Health, and then amplify damage they take by 15% for 4 seconds (90s cooldown).' Introduces a new trigger, "manualActiveBurst" (see ItemTrigger.ManualActiveBurst / Combo.ComboEngine.ApplyAttachedItemEffects): unlike every other item in this file, this one is NOT auto-applied across the whole build (it is not an on-hit/spellblade/stack-then-consume proc) -- it only fires on the single combo node the user drag-attaches it to (ComboNode.AttachedItemId), which was previously a UX/organization-only sub-icon with zero engine effect (see M04_COMBO_EDITOR.md loop-38 LEAD DECISION). targetMaxHpPercent (0.15) becomes a new trailing flat magic-damage node keyed to that node (never folded into the attached node's own damage number, since its type -- Magic -- may differ from whatever type that node's own skill/AA damage already is). amplifyDamagePercent (0.15) / amplifyDurationSeconds (4) describe the target-side 'increased damage taken' debuff: every OTHER node in the same combo whose own elapsed-time-in-combo timestamp falls within 4 seconds after the attached node has its damage multiplied by 1.15 -- this generically boosts ANY subsequent damage in that window (abilities, on-hit procs, already-curated burn/DoT sources like Brand's passive or Cassiopeia's Q), matching the item's real debuff (it amplifies damage taken from any source, not just this item's own burst). The 90s cooldown is not modeled (single-application-per-combo, consistent with this project's existing spellblade/manual-rune 'at most once per combo' convention). Re-check this note against the bundled item.json (or a live wiki fetch) whenever the game version this project targets changes.
3128.name: Deathfire Grasp
